In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of the pathologies associated with FTLD‐tau, FTLD‐TDB and motor neuron disease (MND), with the aim of identifying potential therapeutic targets for these diseases.
the development of a novel, rapid and reliable assay for the detection of TDP‐43 and tau in human brain tissue and CSF.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tau and TDP-43 pathologies can be seen together in the brain in either FTLD or MND.
tau and TDP-43 proteinopathies do not interact, and that the presence of one does not cause the presence of the other, and vice versa.
dual proteinopathies are rare, and when they do occur, they do not interact.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dual proteinopathy is more common in inherited FTLD, but is also present in a small subset of sporadic FTLD cases, and is more common in FTLD‐TARDBP than FTLD‐MAPT cases.
tau‐ and TDP‐pathology can be found in the same cell, but they do not interact with each other.
dual pathology is not a feature of sporadic FTLD or sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dual proteinopathy in FTLD is not associated with an earlier age of onset, a more aggressive disease or a more rapid rate of cognitive decline.
dual proteinopathy is not a common feature in FTLD or motor neurone diseases.
tau pathology is not a feature of TDP‐43 pathology in either FTLD or MND.
